arxiv-2103-13330.title: Convergence Rate Analysis for Deep Ritz Method This work has been presented at workshop on ”Data Driven Scientific Computing” held in Southern University of Science and Technology, China, on November 21-22, 2020.
arxiv-2103-13330.creator: Chenguang Duan, Yuling Jiao, Yanming Lai, Xiliang Lu, Jerry Zhijian Yang
arxiv-2103-13330.description: Abstract Using deep neural networks to solve PDEs has attracted a lot of attentions recently. However, why the deep learning method works is falling far behind its empirical success. In this paper, we provide a rigorous numerical analysis on deep Ritz method (DRM) [ 48 ] for second order elliptic equations with Neumann boundary conditions.

arxiv-2107-07182.title: Hierarchical single-ion anisotropies in spin-1 Heisenberg antiferromagnets on the honeycomb lattice
arxiv-2107-07182.creator: Nils Caci, Lukas Weber, Stefan Wessel
arxiv-2107-07182.description: Abstract We examine the thermal properties of the spin-1 Heisenberg antiferromagnet on the honeycomb lattice in the presence of an easy-plane single-ion anisotropy as well as the effects of an additional weak in-plane easy-axis anisotropy. In particular, using large-scale quantum Monte Carlo simulations, we analyze the scaling of the correlation length near the thermal phase transition into the ordered phase.

arxiv-2110-01720.title: Separation of Artifacts from Spin-Torque Ferromagnetic Resonance Measurements of Spin-Orbit Torque for the Low-Symmetry van der Waals Semi-Metal ZrTe 3
arxiv-2110-01720.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by . Spin-orbit torques generated by exfoliated layers of the low-symmetry semi-metal ZrTe 3 are measured using the spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance (ST-FMR) technique. When the ZrTe 3 has a thickness greater than about 10 nm, artifacts due to spin pumping and/or resonant heating can cause the standard ST-FMR analysis to overestimate the true magnitude of the torque efficiency by as much as a factor of 30, and to indicate incorrectly that the spin-orbit torque depends strongly on the ZrTe 3 layer thickness.

arxiv-2208-09287.title: Detect to Learn: Structure Learning with Attention and Decision Feedback for MIMO-OFDM Receive Processing
arxiv-2208-09287.creator: Jiarui Xu, Lianjun Li, Lizhong Zheng, Lingjia Liu
arxiv-2208-09287.description: Abstract The limited over-the-air (OTA) pilot symbols in multiple-input-multiple-output orthogonal-frequency-division-multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) systems presents a major challenge for detecting transmitted data symbols at the receiver, especially for machine learning-based approaches. While it is crucial to explore effective ways to exploit pilots, one can also take advantage of the data symbols to improve detection performance.

arxiv-2208-11440.title: Dynamic Template Initialization for Part-Aware Person Re-ID
arxiv-2208-11440.creator: Kalana Abeywardena, Shechem Sumanthiran, Sanoojan Baliah, Nadarasar Bahavan, Nalith Udugampola, Ajith Pasqual, Chamira Edussooriya, Ranga Rodrigo
arxiv-2208-11440.description: Abstract Many of the existing Person Re-identification (Re-ID) approaches depend on feature maps which are either partitioned to localize parts of a person or reduced to create a global representation. While part localization has shown significant success, it uses either naïve position-based partitions or static feature templates.

arxiv-2211-11873.title: Effects of physical and chemical pressure on charge density wave transitions in LaAg 1-x Au x Sb 2 single crystals
arxiv-2211-11873.creator: Li Xiang 1, , Dominic H. Ryan 1,2 , Paul C. Canfield 1 and Sergey L. Bud’ko 1
arxiv-2211-11873.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Li Xiang 1, , Dominic H. Ryan 1,2 , Paul C. Canfield 1 and Sergey L. Bud’ko 1. The structural characterization and electrical transport measurements at ambient and applied pressures of the compounds of the La(Ag 1-x Au x )Sb 2 family are presented.

arxiv-2309-06831.title: Spectral Analysis of the LMXB XTE J1810–189 with NICER Data 2022 Spectral Analysis of the LMXB XTE J1810–189 with NICER Data – References
arxiv-2309-06831.creator: A. Manca, A. Sanna, A. Marino, T. Di Salvo, S. M. Mazzola, A. Riggio, N. Deiosso, C. Cabras, L. Burderi
arxiv-2309-06831.description: Abstract XTE J1810–189 is a Low-Mass X-ray Binary transient system hosting a neutron star, which underwent a three-month-long outburst in 2020. In order to study its spectral evolution during this outburst, we analysed all the available observations performed by NICER , in the 1–10 keV energy band. Firstly, we fitted the spectra with a thermal Comptonisation model.

arxiv-2311-11951.title: An Improved Quantum Private Set Intersection Protocol Based on Hadamard Gates
arxiv-2311-11951.creator: Wen-Jie Liu 1,2, Wen-Bo Li 1, Hai-Bin Wang 1,2
arxiv-2311-11951.description: Abstract Recently, Liu and Yin (Int. J. Theor. Phys. 60, 2074-2083 (2021)) proposed a two-party private set intersection protocol based on quantum Fourier transform. We find the participant can deduce the other party’s private information, which violates the security requirement of private set computation.

arxiv-2408-16942.title: A longitudinal sentiment analysis of Sinophobia during COVID-19 using large language models Journal: .
arxiv-2408-16942.creator: Chen Wang, Rohitash Chandra
arxiv-2408-16942.description: Abstract The COVID-19 pandemic has exacerbated xenophobia, particularly Sinophobia, leading to widespread discrimination against individuals of Chinese descent. Large language models (LLMs) are pre-trained deep learning models used for natural language processing (NLP) tasks. The ability of LLMs to understand and generate human-like text make them particularly useful for analyzing social media data to detect and evaluate sentiments.

arxiv-2507-03094.title: Neural Dynamic Modes: Computational Imaging of Dynamical Systems from Sparse Observations
arxiv-2507-03094.creator: Ali SaraerToosi, Renbo Tu, Kamyar Azizzadenesheli, Aviad Levis
arxiv-2507-03094.description: Abstract Dynamical systems are ubiquitous within science and engineering, from turbulent flow across aircraft wings to structural variability of proteins. Although some systems are well understood and simulated, scientific imaging often confronts never‑before‑seen dynamics observed through indirect, noisy, and highly sparse measurements.

arxiv-2508-06102.title: Mass Spectrum of Heavy Mesons using WKB Approximation
arxiv-2508-06102.creator: Bhaskar Jyoti Hazarika, Tanmay Dev
arxiv-2508-06102.description: Abstract In this study, we analyze the bound-state energy spectrum of quark-antiquark systems using the semiclassical WKB approximation. We consider the Cornell potential, which combines a linear confinement term with a Coulombic interaction, and perform a Taylor series expansion around an appropriately chosen point r 0 r_{0} to simplify the potential near the classical turning points.

arxiv-2509-01793.title: Toward a Unified Benchmark and Taxonomy of Stochastic Environments
arxiv-2509-01793.creator: Aryan Amit Barsainyan, Jing Yu Lim, Dianbo Liu
arxiv-2509-01793.description: Abstract Reinforcement Learning (RL) agents have achieved strong results on benchmarks such as Atari100k, yet they remain limited in robustness to real-world conditions. Model-Based RL approaches that rely on learned World Models often struggle in environments with true stochasticity and partial observability, despite their theoretical grounding in POMDPs.

arxiv-2511-05783.title: Stability of parabolic equations in non-cylindrical domains
arxiv-2511-05783.creator: Lingyang Liu
arxiv-2511-05783.description: Abstract This paper addresses the stability of a class of parabolic equations in non-cylindrical domains. We investigate the L ∞ L^{\infty} -stability of systems for both nondegenerate and degenerate cases. Unlike in cylindrical domains, solutions to such problems may not exhibit exponential decay.

arxiv-2601-12093.title: PTL-PINNs: Perturbation-Guided Transfer Learning with Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Nonlinear Systems Journal: Journal of Computational Physics
arxiv-2601-12093.creator: Duarte Alexandrino, Ben Moseley, Pavlos Protopapas
arxiv-2601-12093.description: Abstract Accurately and efficiently solving nonlinear differential equations is crucial for modeling dynamic behavior across science and engineering. Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have emerged as a powerful solution that embeds physical laws in training by enforcing equation residuals. However, these struggle to model nonlinear dynamics, suffering from limited generalization across problems and long training times.

arxiv-2602-07593.title: Beyond Arrow: From Impossibility to Possibilities in Multi-Criteria Benchmarking
arxiv-2602-07593.creator: Polina Gordienko, Christoph Jansen, Julian Rodemann, Georg Schollmeyer
arxiv-2602-07593.description: Abstract Modern benchmarks such as HELM MMLU account for multiple metrics like accuracy, robustness and efficiency. When trying to turn these metrics into a single ranking, natural aggregation procedures can become incoherent or unstable to changes in the model set.

pmc-12464220.title: Identification of genes related to the effects of bicalutamide and zoladex on benign prostatic hyperplasia
pmc-12464220.creator: Guohui Peng, Zicun Liang, Fei Zuo, Jiuming Li, Fei Han, Bin Zhang, Hua Shen
pmc-12464220.description: Existing research indicates that bicalutamide and zoladex show significant potential in treating prostate cancer. However, in the clinical application of treating benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), it is limited due to relatively severe side effects, and the specific mechanism of action has not been fully studied.

pmc-12575272.title: Circadian system and aging: where both times interact
pmc-12575272.creator: Claudia García Cobarro, Lara Ignez Soares, Yevheniy Kutsenko, Antonia Tomas-Loba
pmc-12575272.description: Time shapes life both through its steady progression, as seen in aging, and through its eternal return, reflected in biological rhythms. These two temporal forces have sculpted organisms from their evolutionary beginnings, intertwining the processes of circadian regulation and senescence into the emerging concept of circadian aging.

pmc-12613479.title: Mechanism of methyltransferase METTL14 mediating m6A modification and regulating SIRT5 expression to promote ferroptosis and repress gastric cancer progression
pmc-12613479.creator: Haoruo Zhang, Yi Jia, Kaiqing Guo, Zhe Bai
pmc-12613479.description: ObjectivesGastric cancer (GC) ranks as the third leading reason of cancer-associated deaths worldwide. This study investigates the mechanism by which the m6A methyltransferase methyltransferase-like 14 (METTL14) enhances ferroptosis and inhibits GC progression through regulation of sirtuin 5 (SIRT5).MethodsIn vitro, AGS cells were treated with pcDNA3.1–METTL14, si-SIRT5 and Ferrostatin-1, while NCI-N87 cells were transfected with si-METTL14.

pmc-12720016.title: Cladistic Relationships and Landscape Genetics of the Endangered Indian Peacock Softshell Turtle Nilssonia hurum (Gray, 1830): Implications for Strategic Conservation Planning
pmc-12720016.creator: Imon Abedin, Angkasa Putra, Hye‐Eun Kang, Arunima Singh, Shailendra Singh, Hilloljyoti Singha, Hyun‐Woo Kim, Shantanu Kundu
pmc-12720016.description: The endangered Peacock Softshell Turtle Nilssonia hurum (Gray, 1830) has undergone a steep population decline in recent decades because of habitat loss and anthropogenic pressures, highlighting the urgent need for scientific intervention to ensure its protection in the wild. Thus, the present study integrates mitogenomic and ecological data to guide proactive conservation strategies for this species.

pmc-13052743.title: Strategies for prevention, early detection and management of penile and testicular cancer in primary healthcare: scoping review protocol
pmc-13052743.creator: Ricardo Souza Evangelista Sant’Ana, Widson Davi Vaz de Matos, Juliana Bezerra do Amaral Amaral, Sabine Calleja, Christine Maheu, Nicolas H Hart, Ariana Luiza Rabelo, Anderson Reis de Sousa
pmc-13052743.description: IntroductionTo address the global increase in cancer incidence, improving prevention strategies, early detection and management of bowel and testicular cancer in primary healthcare can improve clinical decisions. Although national efforts are aligned with global health agendas, there is no consolidated evidence to support effective actions.

uslaw-usc-t30-s615.title: 30 U.S.C. § 615 — Limitation of existing rights
uslaw-usc-t30-s615.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t30-s615.description: United States Code, Title 30 (Mineral Lands And Mining); Chapter 15 (Surface Resources); Subchapter II (Mining Locations). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Nothing in this subchapter and sections 601 and 603 of this title shall be construed in any manner to limit or restrict or to authorize the limitation or restriction of any existing rights of any claimant under any valid mining.
